records.source_rule: A Locked player can discard a non-critical clued card as Sacrifice Discard in a dire position without implying Sarcastic or Gentleman's Discard.
records.critical_variable: Bob is Locked, red 3 is non-critical, and the position is dire.
records.blind_answer: Treat the discard as Sacrifice Discard, not Sarcastic or Gentleman's Discard.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: The explicit Sacrifice exception applies to this locked non-critical discard.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Force Sarcastic or Gentleman's meaning; the source says Sacrifice does not imply either.
records.mutation: Make red 3 critical and sacrificing it is no longer licensed by this rule.
records.noise: The post-discard state puts red 3 in discard history rather than leaving it in Bob's hand.

records.source_rule: After a Scream, if obeying the no-discard rule would spend the last clue and force the next Locked player to lose a critical card, the screamed-at player keeps the Chop Move and makes a Rebellious Discard from new chop.
records.learning_objective: Override the ordinary post-Scream no-discard rule only for the downstream emergency.
records.critical_variable: Using the generated clue leaves Locked Cathy at zero clues and forces a critical discard.
records.blind_answer: Make a Rebellious Discard from the new chop.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: Spending the clue creates the immediate critical loss the exception is designed to prevent.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Waste the clue as normal; Cathy then loses a critical card.
records.mutation: Give Cathy a safe action and the Rebellious necessity disappears.
records.noise: The Solution shows Bob's post-Scream Chop Moved state without action-storyboard labels.

records.source_rule: Echo Scream bounces through each consecutive player with a known play or known safe discard, Chop Moving them and the next unsafe player.
records.critical_variable: Bob and Cathy are both safe before Donald, the first unsafe player.
records.blind_answer: Three Chop Moves: Bob, Cathy, and Donald.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: Each safe player adds one bounce before the Scream reaches the unsafe player.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Stop after Bob or Cathy; that contradicts the consecutive-bounce rule.
records.mutation: Remove Cathy's safe action and the chain shortens.
records.noise: Only the safe-action facts needed for the count are shown.

records.source_rule: Shout Discards cannot cause Echo Chop Moves; known-trash discard is only a single Shout Discard Chop Move or Generation Discard.
records.learning_objective: Keep the Echo mechanic exclusive to Scream severity.
records.critical_variable: Alice discarded globally known trash rather than making an unknown-card Scream.
records.blind_answer: The team must reject an Echo Shout interpretation.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: The source explicitly prohibits Echo from Shout Discards.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Bounce through Bob because he is safe; the severity rule rejects that.
records.mutation: Make the emergency discard a genuine Scream and Echo can become possible.
records.noise: Known-trash status and Bob's safe action are the only contrast facts needed.

records.source_rule: If Bob has no safe action and has an important chop while Cathy already has a safe action, Alice's emergency discard is Scream to Bob; Bob Chop Moves and may not discard that turn.
records.learning_objective: Choose the Scream branch of the Level 22 flowchart and preserve the no-discard consequence.
records.critical_variable: Bob has critical chop and no safe action while Cathy already has a known play.
records.blind_answer: Treat it as Scream, mark yellow 5 Chop Moved, and do not discard.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: Generation for Cathy is unnecessary because Cathy already has a safe action.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Discard after moving chop; the ordinary Scream rule forbids that.
records.mutation: Remove Cathy's safe action and give her the critical chop; Generation can become the right branch.
records.noise: The Question is already after Alice's discard with one clue available.

records.source_rule: A genuine last-resort Scream aimed past a next player who already has a safe action Echoes, Chop Moving both the safe next player and the following endangered player.
records.learning_objective: Recognize the two-player Echo Scream case.
records.critical_variable: Bob already has a known play while Cathy has critical chop.
records.blind_answer: Bob and Cathy both have their chop cards marked Chop Moved.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: A last-resort Scream only to already-safe Bob would be pointless.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Move only Bob's chop; that fails to explain the last-resort discard.
records.mutation: Remove Bob's safe action and ordinary Scream to Bob becomes sufficient.
records.noise: Russian wording treats Chop Moved as a state rather than a verb calque.

records.source_rule: Teams should not bend over backwards with Scream to save a Phantom Playable, especially a 4, when connectors are not ready and other critical chops compete for resources.
records.learning_objective: Apply the deliberately non-absolute Phantom protection rule.
records.critical_variable: The Phantom card is a 4, connectors are unclued, and another critical chop needs attention.
records.blind_answer: Do not risk a Scream solely to preserve Bob's Phantom red 4.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: The source explicitly allows losing Phantom cards in tight cases, especially 4s.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Scream to save the Phantom card; that overprotects it at unacceptable risk.
records.mutation: Make the Phantom card lower and the connectors immediately clueable with no competing critical chop; Scream protection becomes more reasonable.
records.noise: The visible connector and competing-chop facts are all relevant to the judgment.

records.source_rule: When Bob has no safe action but Cathy has an important chop and no safe action, Alice's emergency discard can be Generation so Bob uses the new clue to protect Cathy's card rather than Chop Moving himself.
records.learning_objective: Choose the Generation branch of the flowchart.
records.critical_variable: Cathy's yellow 5 is critical and she has no safe action.
records.blind_answer: Use the generated clue to save Cathy's yellow 5.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: Chop Moving Bob ignores the actual endangered card the generated clue can save.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Treat it as Scream to Bob; that is the wrong branch given Cathy's critical chop.
records.mutation: Give Cathy a known play and make Bob's own chop critical; the answer can flip toward Scream to Bob.
records.noise: Post-discard clue count and Cathy's rank-5 chop make the decision state explicit.

records.source_rule: Phantom Playable protection is desirable but not absolute and loses priority to genuinely critical cards in tight positions.
records.learning_objective: Prioritize true criticality over Phantom convenience.
records.critical_variable: Only one clue exists and Bob's yellow 5 is genuinely critical.
records.blind_answer: Spend the clue protecting Bob's critical yellow 5, not Cathy's Phantom red 4.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: Save Principle protects the truly critical card while Phantom protection is explicitly defeasible.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Save the Phantom red 4; that risks losing the unique yellow 5.
records.mutation: Make Bob's yellow 5 non-critical and Phantom protection can become the better use of the clue.
records.noise: Bob's rank-5 chop is inherently critical; visible connectors establish Cathy's Phantom status.

records.source_rule: A card playable only through visible connectors that are neither clued nor in Finesse Position is Phantom Playable, not Delayed Playable, and cannot receive a Play Clue yet.
records.learning_objective: Distinguish Phantom from Delayed Playable by connector status.
records.critical_variable: Bob's red 2 and red 3 are visible but unclued and not in Finesse Position.
records.blind_answer: Alice must not give Cathy's Phantom red 4 a Play Clue yet.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: Delayed Playable requires clued or Finesse-position connectors.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Give red 4 a Play Clue immediately; the source forbids this for Phantom cards.
records.mutation: Clue red 2 and red 3 first and red 4 can become delayed playable.
records.noise: The two visible connector cards are the only distinction being tested.

records.source_rule: The Level 22 Scream flowchart intentionally leaves a branch unclassified when Bob is safe but the following player's chop is ordinary and not one of the important categories.
records.learning_objective: Respect the flowchart boundary instead of fabricating an Echo or Generation label.
records.critical_variable: Cathy has no safe action but her chop is ordinary: not unique playable, critical, or unique 2.
records.blind_answer: Bob must not force a standard Echo or Generation classification; he must reason from the actual position.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: The source flowchart explicitly terminates this branch as advanced or unclassified, or a possible mistake.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Assign Echo or Generation mechanically; that is unsupported beyond the chart boundary.
records.mutation: Make Cathy's chop critical and the standard Echo branch becomes available.
records.noise: Only Bob's safe action and Cathy's ordinary chop classification are needed.
